name: Degrees of Food Uncleanness (Rishon, Sheni, Shlishi)
notes: The graduated system of food impurity: first, second, third (and fourth for kodesh), how they interact, combine, and are transmitted; central topic of Taharot tractate

name: Combination of Foods for Minimum Measure (Tziruf)
notes: Rules for combining different pieces of food to meet the minimum bulk (egg-size) required for conveying or contracting impurity, including foods of different grades

name: Doubtful Impurity in Private vs. Public Domain
hebrew: ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד ורשות הרבים
notes: The fundamental rule that doubtful impurity in a private domain is deemed unclean while in a public domain it is deemed clean; distinctions between domains for purposes of impurity law

name: Am HaAretz and Chaver in Laws of Purity
notes: Rules governing the presumed impurity of an am haaretz and the effect of leaving objects in their possession; the chaver's practices of purity and their interaction with am haaretz

name: Susceptibility to Impurity of Olives and Grapes
notes: When olives and grapes become susceptible to impurity through their liquids during pressing; debates between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on the stages of preparation

name: Neveilah of a Clean Bird (Neveilat Of HaTahor)
notes: Special impurity rules for the carcass of a clean bird: intention requirement, gullet defilement, sanctuary entry guilt, terumah burning, and effect of slaughtering or melikah

name: Liquids as Conveyors and Connectors of Impurity
notes: Rules about liquids serving as connectors (tziruf) between objects for impurity transmission; flow between vessels, dripping moisture as connective; outer surfaces of vessels and liquids

name: Doubtful Contact with Sheretz
notes: Rules for doubtful contact with a dead sheretz in public and private domains, including moving sheretz, weasel carrying sheretz, and sheretz found in various contexts

name: Status of Impurity Determined at Time of Discovery
notes: Principle that all cases of doubtful impurity are assessed according to their condition at the time they are found (e.g., needle found rusty is clean)

name: Testimony and Witness Credibility in Impurity Cases
notes: Rules on when one or two witnesses are believed regarding impurity, including conflict between witnesses, self-testimony, and testimony of women in purity contexts

name: Midras Impurity from Am HaAretz
notes: Clothes and objects left with or exposed to an am haaretz are presumed to have midras (pressure) impurity; rules for deposits with am haaretz

name: Beit HaPras Doubtful Impurity Cases
notes: Among the six doubtful impurity cases for which terumah is burned; the specific rules of beit hapras as a source of doubtful corpse impurity

name: Purity Standards in Olive Press and Wine Press
notes: Detailed rules for maintaining purity during olive and grape pressing; workers' movements, trusted/untrusted persons, cleansing of press vessels

name: Designation as Food (Machshavah) for Susceptibility to Impurity
notes: Whether designation (intention) for human consumption renders an object susceptible to food impurity; role of intent vs. act in making food susceptible; deaf-mute and minor's intention
